topics.name: ITAM Overview & Fundamentals
topics.description: IT asset management basics, hardware asset lifecycle, implementation best practices, personas and roles.

introduction.overview: ITAM Fundamentals covers the core concepts of IT Asset Management and Hardware Asset Management in ServiceNow, including asset lifecycle stages, ITAM personas and roles, and implementation best practices.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain represents 20% of the CIS-HAM exam. Questions cover ITAM terminology, hardware asset lifecycle stages, HAM personas (Asset Manager, Procurement, etc.), ITSM Asset Management vs HAM capabilities, and implementation methodology.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the hardware asset lifecycle from planning through disposal. Know the difference between ITSM Asset Management (foundation) and HAM (advanced capabilities). Master the key personas and their responsibilities in the ITAM program.
introduction.examTips: ITSM Asset Management is included with ITSM licenses; HAM requires additional licensing. The asset lifecycle includes Plan, Acquire, Deploy, Operate, Retire, and Dispose phases. Know which features require which plugins.

topics.name: Data Integrity & Sources
topics.description: Trustworthy data, assets vs CIs, hardware discovery, normalization, and Hardware Model Normalization.

introduction.overview: Data Integrity covers how hardware data flows into ServiceNow, the relationship between assets and configuration items (CIs), Discovery integration, and Hardware Model Normalization for creating accurate hardware models.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 27% of the exam. Expect questions on assets vs CIs, Discovery integration, CI to asset relationships, Hardware Model Normalization, Normalization Data Services, and data synchronization between CMDB and Asset tables.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the difference between assets (financial) and CIs (technical). Master how Discovery populates the CMDB and triggers asset creation. Know how Hardware Model Normalization standardizes model data and provides lifecycle information.
introduction.examTips: Assets track financial data (cost, depreciation); CIs track technical data. Not all CIs are assets, and not all assets are CIs. Hardware Model Normalization matches discovered hardware to normalized models. The Content Service provides model lifecycle data.

topics.name: Practical Asset Management
topics.description: Consumables, inventory and stock, automation, asset flows, tasks, contract management, and retirement.

introduction.overview: Practical Asset Management covers day-to-day HAM operations including consumable tracking, inventory and stock management, automated asset flows and tasks, contract lifecycle, and asset retirement processes.
introduction.whyItMatters: This is the largest domain at 30% of the exam. Questions focus on consumable management, inventory tracking, stock rules, transfer orders, asset flows for automation, asset tasks, contract management, and the retirement/disposal process.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the difference between assets and consumables. Master inventory tracking with stockrooms and transfer orders. Know how asset flows automate lifecycle transitions with tasks. Understand the retirement process and disposal options.
introduction.examTips: Consumables are tracked by quantity, not individually. Stock rules trigger automatic reordering. Asset flows define the sequence of tasks for lifecycle events. Retirement moves assets through states before final disposal.

topics.name: Operational Integration
topics.description: Reports, dashboards, Hardware Asset Workspace, requests, procurement, data certification, and hygiene.

introduction.overview: Operational Integration covers HAM reporting and dashboards, the Hardware Asset Workspace for asset managers, request and procurement workflows, and data quality management through certification and hygiene processes.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 18% of the exam. Questions cover HAM dashboards and reports, Hardware Asset Workspace features, service catalog integration for asset requests, procurement workflows, data certification, and data hygiene processes.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master the Hardware Asset Workspace layout and capabilities. Know how to create and interpret HAM reports and dashboards. Understand procurement integration from request to receiving. Know how data certification and hygiene maintain data quality.
introduction.examTips: Hardware Asset Workspace provides a unified view for asset managers. Procurement can auto-create assets from purchase orders. Data certification validates asset data periodically. Data hygiene rules identify and remediate quality issues.

topics.name: Financial Management
topics.description: Hardware contract financials, rate cards, expense lines, depreciation, fixed assets, and total cost of ownership.

introduction.overview: Financial Management covers the financial aspects of hardware asset management, including contract cost tracking, depreciation calculations, fixed asset integration, and total cost of ownership analysis.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain is 5% of the exam. Questions cover hardware contract financials, rate cards for cost allocation, expense line processing, depreciation methods, fixed asset synchronization, and TCO calculation.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand how contracts track financial obligations. Know rate cards for cost allocation. Master depreciation methods (straight-line, declining balance). Understand fixed asset integration for financial reporting and TCO components.
introduction.examTips: Rate cards define costs for contract items. Depreciation reduces asset value over time for accounting. Fixed assets integration syncs with financial systems. TCO includes acquisition, operation, and disposal costs.
